name: Global smallpox eradication programme
description: A coordinated international public-health programme combined vaccination and surveillance; the World Health Assembly declared eradication in 1980.

date.basis: Source date for the documented context; BP conversion uses 1950 as reference where applicable.

events.statement: WHO launched an intensified smallpox eradication programme in 1967.

evidence.supports: WHO describes a global programme involving health workers, national participation and vaccination, and reports the 1980 World Health Assembly declaration. Its half-billion vaccination figure is a programme-level claim rather than a unique-person count.

events.caveats: Programme activities, national contexts and individual experiences varied; the declaration concerns natural disease transmission, and the campaign is distinct from the earlier development of vaccination.

measures.subject: Global campaign
measures.conditions: WHO’s round estimate for the roughly decade-long eradication effort; vaccinations are not necessarily distinct persons.

evidence.supports: WHO describes a global programme involving health workers, national participation and vaccination, and reports the 1980 World Health Assembly declaration. Its half-billion vaccination figure is a programme-level claim rather than a unique-person count.

measures.subject: Global smallpox eradication programme
measures.conditions: WHO’s retrospective estimate for 1967–1980; no price base or inflation adjustment is specified. WHO says about two thirds was borne by endemic countries.

evidence.supports: WHO estimates the 1967–1980 programme cost at US$300 million and reports that endemic countries bore about two thirds.

links.statement: The eradication programme built on the smallpox vaccination approach associated with Jenner and combined vaccination with surveillance.
links.scope: Historical relationship between vaccination as a preventive approach and the later international programme; not a claim of an unchanged formulation.
links.caveats: Vaccines, delivery systems and programme strategies changed over the intervening period.

evidence.supports: WHO identifies Jenner’s 1796 vaccination as an early preventive approach and vaccination as part of the global eradication programme.
